incident_report.incident: Bumped on jumping and then shortly after the start was steadied when crowded between JOLLY JUMPER and SMILING EMPEROR which shifted in.  Crowded after travelling a short distance.  When questioned Y L Chung stated that as the horse does not always begin well it can often settle further back in the field than instructed.  He said today when his mount jumped well he was able to hold a more forward position than it had at its previous race starts.  He added that near the 1200 Metres when JOLLY JUMPER was steadied in front he became awkwardly placed close to that runner which resulted in IRON LEGION becoming unbalanced and blundering at that point.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Between the 450 Metres and the 350 Metres was held up for clear running.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Crowded after travelling a short distance.
Held up on the Home Turn.
No report.

Bumped on jumping.  After travelling a short distance SMILING EMPEROR shifted in and away from SILVER KING (H T Mo) after SILVER KING shifted in before being corrected by Jockey Mo.  As a consequence IRON LEGION, DRACO and STRONGEST BOY were all steadied when crowded to the inside of SMILING EMPEROR.  H T Mo was reprimanded and advised in similar circumstances he would be expected to correct his mount sooner than what he did on this occasion.
After being crossed by SMILING EMPEROR near the 800 Metres raced keenly for some distance thereafter.
Bumped on jumping.  Over the final 200 Metres raced tight between IRON LEGION and PANDA LEGEND, both of which shifted ground.
No report.
No report.

Noted to have blood in the mouth on arrival at the Start, was examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race.  Raced keenly in the early and middle stages.  When questioned K Teetan stated that his mount hung out in the middle stages.  He said near the 450 Metres he endeavoured to force a run between SILVER KING and ISLAND GOLDEN but when SILVER KING commenced to give ground at that point he was checked when disappointed for this run.  He added that as a result he remained very awkwardly placed behind SILVER KING between the 450 Metres and the 350 Metres at which point he struck the heels of SILVER KING and blundered badly.  K Teetan was reprimanded and advised in similar circumstances he would be expected to ensure that there is sufficient racing room to improve into runs.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

J Orman stated that the intention was to obtain cover.  He said when SHINE BRIGHT jumped well he was able to hold the lead without being pressured to do so, but, in his opinion, SHINE BRIGHT did not run out the 1600 Metres of today’s race.
Bumped at the start and as a result shifted in and made contact with IRON LEGION.  After travelling a short distance was momentarily crowded by SILVER KING.

Raced wide and without cover from the 800 Metres.  H T Mo reported that he was issued with no specific instruction other than to have the horse race where comfortable, particularly as it is a known "roarer”.  He said when SILVER KING jumped well today he was able to hold a more forward position than at its previous race starts.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race found that horse to be a "roarer” which had previously been reported.  The performance of SILVER KING, which finished tailed out, was considered unacceptable.  Before being allowed to race again, SILVER KING will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

When questioned regarding the improved performance Trainer W Y So stated that the horse was advantaged by having experience at its first race start and further was assisted by receiving a comfortable run in the lead, particularly in the middle stages of the event.  Sent for sampling post-race.

No report. <4/1/2026 1 January 2026 Sha Tin Racemeeting – Race 7 (309)> The Stewards today interviewed Jockeys J Orman, rider of THE LION KING, and L Ferraris, rider of GLORIASTAR, in relation to GLORIASTAR obtaining a position with cover approaching the first turn and then THE LION KING being able to improve three deep when GLORIASTAR shifted out on the Home Turn.  J Orman stated that approaching the first turn when following KINGLY DEMEANOR he elected to allow his mount to shift to the rail when GLORIASTAR improved to his outside and applied some pressure to his mount.  He said his decision to shift to the rail was also influenced by the fact that he was able to follow FRANTANCK and improve his position slightly as he did so and to provide his mount with an uninterrupted run.  He added making the Home Turn he was able to shift to the outside of KINGLY DEMEANOR to obtain clear running as he felt GLORIASTAR was not travelling well enough to hold its position at that stage.  L Ferraris stated that approaching the first turn he was looking to obtain cover behind KINGLY DEMEANOR and as a result turned his horse’s head in to endeavour to influence THE LION KING to the rail.  He said after obtaining a position behind KINGLY DEMEANOR his mount came under pressure from the 500 Metres and he was unable to prevent THE LION KING from shifting out on the Home Turn.

Improved into a tight run near the 300 Metres and then became unbalanced when crowded between CALIFORNIA BANNER and GLORIASTAR.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

When questioned H Bowman stated that throughout the early and middle stages of the event his mount was obliged to race wide and without cover, however, raced tractably during that section of the race.  He said in the Home Straight when positioned to the outside of HAPPY INDEX his mount commenced to lay in when he urged it forward, however, he was able to maintain a reasonably straight course.  He said once CROSSBORDERPEGASUS improved past HAPPY INDEX it hung in which required him to stop riding and place significant pressure to his left rein to prevent it from shifting in and causing interference which resulted in CROSSBORDERPEGASUS becoming unbalanced and losing momentum at that point.  He added that after he was able to pull his whip through to his right hand near the 100 Metres CROSSBORDERPEGASUS finished the race off reasonably well although it did lay in.  When questioned regarding the carriage of his whip in the left hand H Bowman stated that as it is his preference to carry the whip in his left hand he decided that he would do so during the running of this race.  He said when the horse initially hung in he did not believe it was necessary to pull the whip through as his focus was on maintaining a straight course and, in his opinion, the fact that he carried his whip in his left hand in the early stages of the race had no effect on his ability to ride the horse out as he was able to pull it through to his right hand near the 100 Metres in his usual manner.  Trainer J Size stated that the horse had competed in 4 barrier trials leading up to today’s first up performance where he and the Stewards had been satisfied with the horse’s racing manners.  After considering the matter the Stewards advised Mr Size that CROSSBORDERPEGASUS must barrier trial to the satisfaction of the Stewards from a wide barrier where it would be required to be ridden out in the Home Straight under raceday pressure to the outside of other horses before being allowed to race again.  Sent for sampling post-race.
